content.problem: A prompt edit improves ordinary answers but makes the system confidently answer a question its documents cannot support. Run a bounded local retrieval and deterministic model adapter, trace each stage, and compare candidates on a frozen set of stable case IDs without a paid API.
content.idea: An LLM application combines prompts, retrieved context, a model boundary and infrastructure outcomes. This small local adapter executes retrieval and generation so a trace can show where an answer failed. Its deterministic outputs teach instrumentation and release policy; they are not evidence about a commercial or general-purpose LLM.
objectives: Version the prompt, local retriever, adapter and corpus
Evaluate heterogeneous cases by stable ID
Trace retrieval, prompt, generation and infrastructure outcomes
Localize one failure at each boundary
Compare candidate policies on identical IDs and denominators

sections.title: Trace a response through the system that produced it
sections.body: Follow one request from case inventory to trace. Each record ties a stable case ID to the candidate configuration, prompt, index, retrieved document IDs, adapter input and output, status, and evaluator result. In the baseline run, refund-order-204 fails because retrieval did not deliver the required evidence; case-sensitive-refund-77 reaches the generation boundary but returns a response that breaks its contract; return-ambiguous-9 times out before retrieval or generation. Those three observations point to different owners and fixes. Start with the failed stage in the trace instead of changing the prompt whenever a score drops. This is an executed deterministic local adapter, so its trace explains the fixture run only.

check.prompt: Why retain the retrieved context in an error trace?
check.answer: It distinguishes missing or wrong evidence from generation or instruction-following errors. Without that context, the same final response can support several incompatible diagnoses.

sections.title: Version the application boundary
sections.body: A response depends on several versioned pieces, so give each its own identity. The baseline trace names prompt-v1-careless, index-v1-complete and extractive-local-adapter-v1; its configuration hash is 479424bdd62be245. The candidate uses prompt-v2-grounded and index-v2-complete with the same adapter, under hash 7916d53bb58408ce. Keeping these identities in each trace lets a reviewer ask what actually changed. The recorded retrieval context and adapter response then show how that configuration handled a particular case. For a hosted deployment, also resolve the exact model, tokenizer and serving configuration before comparing runs.

sections.title: Define cases before changing the prompt
sections.body: The \(5\)-case inventory is frozen before the candidate runs: hours-west-17 checks a supported answer, refund-order-204 needs a specific refund document, return-ambiguous-9 exercises a timeout, unsupported-tax-2 requires abstention, and case-sensitive-refund-77 checks answer formatting. The evaluator fixes each expected answer and allowed evidence ID in advance. That means both candidates are scored on the same \(5\) IDs, rather than on whichever requests happened to return. The exact contract is practical for this tiny corpus: it catches a missing document or malformed abstention, but it is not a general semantic judge. Before tuning, list the cases that can change a release decision and the evidence each requires.

sections.title: Read the rare-case failure
sections.body: Read the baseline failures by stage. It passes only hours-west-17, so \(1\) of \(5\) cases passes (\(0.2\)). refund-order-204 lacks its supporting retrieval result; unsupported-tax-2 fails because the careless prompt encourages guessing; case-sensitive-refund-77 has a malformed answer; return-ambiguous-9 times out. The grounded candidate changes the prompt, index and timeout setting, then passes all \(5\) identical IDs (\(5/5\)). This result says the revised fixture configuration satisfies this fixture's contracts. It does not isolate which change caused each improvement: a separate retrieval-only run scores \(0.8\), and a prompt-only run with baseline retrieval and infrastructure settings scores \(3/5\). Use per-case traces and controlled changes to locate cause before making a broad claim about a candidate.

sections.title: Trace enough to diagnose, without retaining everything
sections.body: A useful trace contains enough context to locate a failure: which document IDs were retrieved, what prompt and context reached the adapter, what it returned, and whether execution completed. The sample trace for hours-west-17 records doc-hours and the sentence about Monday through Friday, \(09{:}00\) to \(17{:}00\); the adapter returns that same sentence and the case passes. That is enough to connect the expected evidence to the response. The fixture stores only its own documents. In a real service, prompts and retrieved text can contain private data, so choose redaction, access and retention rules before collecting traces.

sections.title: Add the production cases deliberately
sections.body: Expand the frozen cases to cover missing or contradictory context, multilingual requests, long contexts, prompt injection inside retrieved text, malformed tool arguments, unsupported tools, timeouts and rate limits. For example, retrieved instructions should be treated as untrusted document content, while tool permissions come from an external allowlist. Keep held-out and human-reviewed examples separate from cases used to tune prompts, so the same examples do not serve as both target and evidence of success. If a language-model judge is used, record its version and rubric and compare it with human labels; disagreement identifies cases to inspect.

sections.title: Measure serving work in the right units
sections.body: Choose measurements that match the work being served. Separate prefill from decode, then record time to first token, output tokens per second, completion rate, tail latency and request cost for stated context lengths and concurrency. A whitespace count is not a provider token count, so use the provider's tokenizer and pricing for a cost estimate. Set timeout and retry budgets, and exercise the fallback path. The local adapter records response accounting for the fixture; it cannot establish hosted throughput or provider cost.

commands.label: Run the bounded local adapter experiment
commands.code: Save the lesson experiment as llmops_local.py and run: python llmops_local.py
commands.expected: Executes local retrieval, prompt/model adapter boundaries, stable-ID scoring, diagnostics and candidate comparison. No MLflow installation or model API is required.

sections.title: A missing response is an evaluation failure
sections.body: The scorer expects one outcome for each of the \(5\) frozen IDs. It can join responses by ID even if they arrive out of order, but it rejects duplicate or unknown IDs and keeps a timeout under its original case ID. If a response is missing, that case remains in the denominator and the run cannot quietly improve its score by omitting a failure. In the incomplete-run example, scoring is rejected; dividing only the returned cases would misleadingly report \(0.25\). When comparing two runs, first confirm the expected IDs are all accounted for, then interpret the numerator and denominator.

content.output: Executed local candidate comparison: baseline 1/5 (0.2), candidate 5/5 (1.0), same five stable case IDs and denominator. Traces expose the omitted refund document, correct context with a malformed generated response, unsupported-question hallucination, and a pre-retrieval timeout. Shuffled responses pair by ID; missing, duplicate and unknown IDs are rejected. This adapter is not a hosted LLM or quality benchmark.
content.exercise: Inspect case-sensitive-refund-77 in the baseline trace. Identify the correct retrieval evidence and the prompt behavior that caused the answer to fail, then change only the prompt policy and compare on all five IDs.
content.solution:
trace={t['case_id']:t for t in (json.loads(x) for x in trace_before)}['case-sensitive-refund-77']
assert trace['retrieval']['retrieved_id']=='doc-refund'
assert trace['generation']['model_input_context']==cases[1]['expected']
assert trace['generation']['response'].startswith('Answer: ')
assert trace['diagnosis']=='generation'
# candidate uses all five same IDs; compare only prompt separately by retaining baseline index.
prompt_only=make_candidate('candidate-prompt-only','prompt-v2-grounded','ABSTAIN_WHEN_EMPTY',baseline['index_id'],baseline['index'],excluded=baseline['excluded_docs'],timeouts=baseline['timeouts'],case_excluded=baseline['case_excluded'])
rs=[run_case(case,prompt_only)[0] for case in cases]
paired=score(cases,rs)
assert paired['count']==5 and paired['fraction']==.6
print('Prompt-only score with baseline retrieval and infrastructure settings:',paired['passed'],'/',paired['count'])

experiments.title: Hold the model and prompt fixed while removing one retrieval result
experiments.prediction: The grounded candidate passes all five cases. If only the refund-period case loses its required document, predict the new pass fraction and the trace diagnosis. Should its configuration identity change?
experiments.code:
retrieval_only_config=make_candidate('candidate-drop-one','prompt-v2-grounded','ABSTAIN_WHEN_EMPTY',
    'index-v2-complete',corpus,case_excluded={'refund-order-204':('doc-refund',)})
assert retrieval_only_config['prompt_id']==candidate['prompt_id']
assert retrieval_only_config['model_id']==candidate['model_id']
assert retrieval_only_config['index_id']==candidate['index_id']
assert retrieval_only_config['config_hash']!=candidate['config_hash']
retrieval_only_responses=[]; retrieval_only_traces=[]
for fixed_case in cases:
    response,trace=run_case(fixed_case,retrieval_only_config)
    retrieval_only_responses.append(response);retrieval_only_traces.append(json.loads(trace))
retrieval_only_score=score(cases,retrieval_only_responses)
assert retrieval_only_score['count']==5 and retrieval_only_score['passed']==4
failed_trace=next(t for t in retrieval_only_traces if t['case_id']=='refund-order-204')
assert failed_trace['diagnosis']=='retrieval' and failed_trace['retrieval']['context'] is None
assert sum(not outcome['passed'] for outcome in retrieval_only_score['cases'])==1
print('Retrieval-only change:',retrieval_only_score['fraction'],failed_trace['diagnosis'],
      'config hash changed:',retrieval_only_config['config_hash']!=candidate['config_hash'])
experiments.output: The fraction changes from 1.0 to 0.8; exactly one trace diagnoses missing retrieval evidence. Prompt and model identities are fixed, while the actual retrieval configuration hash changes.
experiments.explanation: The configuration fingerprint includes the excluded documents, per-case exclusions and timeout controls as well as prompt, index and model identity. Identical corpus bytes alone do not identify the executed retrieval configuration. This is a deterministic local adapter, not hosted-LLM quality evidence.

experiments.title: Reject an incomplete case inventory before reporting a score
experiments.prediction: The baseline passes one of five cases. Omitting its unsupported case would make a returned-only ratio \(1/4\) instead of \(1/5\). Should the evaluator report either ratio for an incomplete run?
experiments.output: Reordering preserves all five IDs. The incomplete baseline is rejected before scoring; its misleading returned-only ratio would be 0.25 rather than the complete baseline 0.2.
experiments.explanation: A fixed case inventory is part of the evaluation contract. Missing, duplicate and unknown IDs must be handled before calculating a score, otherwise infrastructure failures can disappear from the denominator.

practice.title: Check abstention structure
practice.prompt: Try a response that claims to abstain but still returns an unsupported answer.
practice.hint: The fixture contract requires both empty answer text and no citations.
practice.solution:
unsupported=next(case for case in cases if not case['supported'])
replies=[run_case(case,candidate)[0] for case in cases]
for reply in replies:
    if reply['id']==unsupported['id']:
        reply['response']='Tax is 15 percent.'
result=score(cases,replies)
failed=next(item for item in result['cases'] if item['id']==unsupported['id'])
assert result['count']==5 and not failed['passed']
print('malformed abstention retained and failed:',failed)
practice.explanation: Validate the full response object; a boolean alone is distinct from that the application withheld an answer.

practice.title: Keep failed work in the evaluation inventory
practice.prompt: Replace the answer for the first answerable case with an empty abstention. Keep the case ID and show how the complete-suite score changes.
practice.hint: Start with the grounded candidate responses. An empty abstention is correct for the unsupported case but wrong for the selected answerable case.
practice.solution:
replies=[run_case(case,candidate)[0] for case in cases]
replies[0]['response']=''
result=score(cases,replies)
assert result['count']==5 and result['passed']==4
assert result['cases'][0]['id']=='hours-west-17' and not result['cases'][0]['passed']
print('failed answer remains in denominator:',result)
practice.explanation: The fixture represents an unsuccessful answer as an empty abstention. A real trace should additionally distinguish timeout, retrieval failure and deliberate abstention as causes, while retaining all cases in the predeclared metric.

content.question: The controlled replay suite passes every case. What is established?
options: The live LLM is safe and accurate for arbitrary requests.
The evaluator accepts these fixtures; live model and held-out application evaluation remain separate.
Prompt versions no longer need recording.
content.explanation: A passing fixture suite establishes that the evaluator accepts those declared cases. It does not establish live application safety, general quality or coverage of unseen prompts. Version the model, prompt, retrieval inputs, tools and evaluator, and keep independent held-out cases.
content.diagnosis: When quality changes, compare prompt/model/retrieval/tool versions and case-level traces before tuning weights. A high average can hide an unsupported-case regression. Do not call a synthetic replay a measured LLM response.
takeaways: Trace enough to diagnose, without retaining everything
Measure serving work in the right units

visual.title: The unsupported case changes the release decision
visual.prediction: How can a candidate pass 90% overall and still fail every unsupported case?
visual.reading: The baseline passes \(1\) of \(5\) fixed cases (\(0.2\)); the grounded candidate passes all \(5\) (\(1.0\)). The bars use the same \(5\) stable IDs, including the unsupported question and the timed-out case, so the rise cannot come from dropping difficult requests.
visual.connection: The candidate changes the prompt and retrieval index while keeping the local adapter and frozen case inventory fixed; it also changes the timeout setting for the injected timeout case. The per-case traces show whether retrieval, generation or infrastructure determined each outcome. The pass fraction describes this deterministic fixture run, not general LLM quality.
visual.alt: The baseline local candidate passes one of five fixed cases; the grounded candidate passes all five on the same stable IDs.
visual.code: visual_data={'kind':'bar','labels':['baseline (5 cases)','grounded candidate (5 cases)'],'xlabel':'candidate (same stable IDs and denominator)','ylabel':'fixture pass fraction','series':[{'label':'observed pass fraction','y':[before['fraction'],after['fraction']]}]}

optionFeedback: Fixtures cover their specified cases, not every live prompt or attack. Preserve scope and add held-out adversarial cases.

A passing fixture suite establishes that the evaluator accepts those declared cases. It does not establish live application safety, general quality or coverage of unseen prompts. Version the model, prompt, retrieval inputs, tools and evaluator, and keep independent held-out cases.
Evaluator success does not remove the need to version prompts, data and models. Record those inputs to make the result reproducible.

inputs: The lesson’s answerable case, its allowed citations, and a response containing an invented citation.
outputs: The evaluator result showing that the unsupported citation fails the case.
invariants: A citation absent from the case’s allowed evidence cannot pass the citation check.
hints: Check citation support against the case evidence, not whether the citation string is well formed.
Keep the test response otherwise valid so the invented citation is the failure cause.
